It’s been about nine months now, ever since the accident, and it still feels like I’m stuck there. I’ll be washing dishes or playing with the kids and suddenly I’m right back in the car, hearing the crash, feeling it in my body. I don’t even mean to think about it; it just slams into my head and I freeze or start crying.

I used to be so on top of everything with the kids and the house, but lately I can’t seem to get myself to do anything. The laundry piles up, I put things off, and then I just sit there staring, feeling useless. I keep thinking if I’d reacted faster, or taken a different route, maybe none of it would’ve happened. It feels like it’s my fault.

I’m on edge all the time. Little things make me snap at my husband or the kids, and then I hate myself for it. My memory’s a mess—I’ll walk into a room and forget why, or misplace things constantly. And if someone touches me from behind, even just my husband brushing past in the kitchen, I jump out of my skin.
